name: SMR and fuel-cell power purchase for data centres
principle: Hyperscalers contract firm clean power at the plant level rather than only grid certificates. Two families lead: advanced reactors sold under long PPAs (Google and Kairos Power's master plant development agreement for up to 500 MW of fluoride-salt-cooled high-temperature reactors, first unit by 2030 and the fleet by 2035, sited in territories serving Google data centres) and on-site solid-oxide fuel cells (Equinix and Bloom Energy's decade-long partnership now above 100 MW across about 19 data centres, running on natural gas today with a hydrogen roadmap). Both convert power procurement from a utility question into a contract-structure question.

process_steps.name: Data centre load profile and clean-energy targets set the requirement
Master plant or PPA structure agreed with the developer
equipment: power purchase agreement with environmental attributes

process_steps.name: Generation built inside or near the serving territory
Firm 24/7 power delivered to the data centre

suppliers.name: Kairos Power
suppliers.product: KP-FHR advanced reactors under master plant development agreements

suppliers.name: Bloom Energy
suppliers.product: solid-oxide fuel cells for on-site data centre power

performance.basis: up to 500 MW by 2035 under a master plant development agreement signed 14 October 2024; first deployment targeted by 2030
more than 100 MW of Bloom solid-oxide fuel cells across about 19 Equinix data centres, under a partnership running since 2015 and expanded in 2025

source.note: The Register, 14 August 2025 (Equinix power deals), read via search summary 2026-11-12

advantages: Firm 24/7 carbon-free power that certificates alone cannot buy
Contract structure (master plant agreements) spreads deployment risk across a fleet
Fuel cells bypass interconnection queues entirely
limitations: Advanced-reactor deployments wait on NRC licensing and first-of-a-kind execution (first unit 2030)
Fuel cells on natural gas carry Scope 3 emissions until hydrogen-ready operation
